ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS STUDIES 
 
GENERAL OBJECTIVES 
 
 
The aim of the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) syllabus in Islamic Studies is 
to prepare the candidates for the Board’s examination.  It is designed to test their achievement of the 
course objectives, which are to: 
1. 
master the Qur’ān and Sunnah as foundations of Islamic and social life; 
2.          be familiar with Islamic heritage, culture and civilization; 
3. 
be acquainted with the tradition of Islamic scholarship and intellectual discourse; 
4. 
demonstrate knowledge of Islamic moral, spiritual, economic, political and social values; 
5. 
be exposed to the fundamental principles of Islam; and  
6. 
be prepared to face the challenges of life as good practising Muslims. 
 
DETAILED SYLLABUS 
 
PART 1: THE QUR’ĀN AND HADĪTH
